svg.aria-label: Compression shrinks the output; bkit stops the re-reading. What a coding agent reads on each request, across 13.5 million GitHub Copilot sessions: 72 percent is re-reading on every request, the conversation so far at 48 percent, the system prompt at 14 percent and instructions and other context at 10 percent, which is what bkit cuts; 28 percent is tool output, all a compressor can touch. The best published compression result on Claude Code took 2.7 percent off the whole bill, and another tool added 48 percent. The model's own writing is about 1 token for every 100 to 275 it reads. Sources: Liu et al., GitHub Copilot at production scale, 2026; Weinberger and Hozez, 2,848 Claude Code runs, 2026; Manus, 2025. An agent's cost is the area under its context line: each request re-sends the whole conversation, and a token costs the same at 900 thousand as at 9 thousand, but a turn at 900 thousand sends 100 times as many. In an illustration of the same work drawn both ways, today one agent runs until about 967 thousand tokens, where Claude Code summarises it and drops detail; bkit hands over to a fresh agent with a short brief in the 80 to 170 thousand band, where practitioners say to start fresh. What published work finds: 11 of 13 models score under half their short-context result by 32 thousand tokens (NoLiMa, ICML 2025); a context should get no more than 40 to 60 percent full before you start a fresh one (HumanLayer, 2025); a sub-agent hands back 1 to 2 thousand tokens from tens of thousands it read (Anthropic, 2025); all 18 models Chroma tested got worse as their context grew. Measure your own runs: bkit records the tokens each agent read in .bkit/stats.jsonl, and bkit stats writes a report of your runs to .bkit/stats.md. How bkit reads less: fresh agents with short briefs, never the whole plan, none past 160 thousand tokens; code does the bookkeeping, so ledger rows, test-first order, summaries and resume points come from bkit commands with the same answer every time; one round, then you decide; each agent carries only its own rules.
